title: Example: coding-session thanks-vs-F-bombs meter
description: A consumer in examples/ (or an optional botspy[metrics] extra) computing the gratitude-vs-profanity meter over BotSpy sessions. Done when: the example runs on fixtures and imports nothing outside the extra.

comments.author: example-user
comments.text: home: Meter example landed at examples/meter/ — scoring.rs holds the gratitude-vs-profanity logic (thanks = 'thanks'/'thank you', F-bombs = censored f***, f**k, or uncensored), main.rs walks the committed synthetic corpus through all five per-agent sources (cargo run --example meter, optional path arg) and prints per-session plus aggregate counts. It imports only botspy and std: examples/meter/scoring.rs is compiled into the BDD step crate via #[path], so scenarios exercise the real example logic and compilation proves public-API-only usage. consumers.feature: @wip moved to the sentiment scenario only; three meter scenarios now executable and green (117 scenarios / 444 steps): per-session counts (2 thanks, 1 F-bomb, ratio favors thanks), cross-session aggregation (1 thanks, 2 F-bombs across 2 sessions), and the public-API/no-added-dependency consumer constraint (import-path whitelist + core Cargo.toml forbidden-dep scan). Also: SQLite WAL sidecars that adapters leave when opening stores in place are now recognized as gitignored runtime artifacts and pruned by the fixture-corpus guards. Full gate green: fmt, clippy -D warnings, doc -D warnings, 8 doc tests, BDD 24 features/117 scenarios/444 steps, spec_docs_coverage, 37 lib tests, fixtures corpus guards, cargo run --example meter.

right_now_summary: The gratitude-versus-profanity meter example is being prepared to run on BotSpy session fixtures.
